question: Given that $\binom{17}{10}=19448$, $\binom{17}{11}=12376$ and $\binom{19}{12}=50388$, find $\binom{18}{12}$.
solution:
By Pascal's identity, C(n,k) = C(n−1,k−1) + C(n−1,k), since a selection either includes a particular item or does not. Thus C(18,11) = C(17,10) + C(17,11) = 19448 + 12376 = 31824. Applying the identity again gives C(19,12) = C(18,11) + C(18,12), so C(18,12) = 50388 − 31824 = 18564.
Final answer: 18564
